description: Cross-topic questions automation testers are asked.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and === and which should test assertions use?
questions.answer:
The loose equality == coerces types before comparing, while strict === requires both type and value to match. Automated assertions should use strict equality so a string and a number never match accidentally.

code:
console.log('42' == 42);   // true
console.log('42' === 42);  // false

real example:
Playwright text matchers compare strings, so converting page text to numbers before toBe comparisons follows the strict-equality rule.

Why should you prefer data-testid selectors over CSS classes in tests?
What is the difference between wait and auto-wait in Playwright?
questions.answer:
Auto-wait means actions retry until the element is actionable within the timeout, checking visibility, stability, and enabled state. Manual waits only sleep or poll once without retry guarantees.

code:
await page.getByRole('button').click();  // auto-waits

real example:
Auto-wait turns a slow-loading modal into a passing test, while page.waitForTimeout can let clicks land before a re-render simply breaks the canvas.

questions.question: How do you handle a popup dialog that appears during a test?
What is the event loop and how does it relate to async test code?
questions.answer:
The event loop coordinates the single-threaded call stack, microtask queue, and macrotask queue so promises and timers run in order. Test awaits compose on it to keep steps ordered.

code:
setTimeout(() => console.log('later'), 0);
console.log('first');  // first, later

real example:
Promise callbacks run before timeout callbacks, which is why an await for a promise result reliably precedes a setTimeout-based poll.

What is the significance of a lockfile such as package-lock.json in CI?
questions.answer:
A lockfile pins exact indirect dependency versions, so npm ci installs the identical tree everywhere and CI results stay reproducible between machines.

code:
npm ci
npx playwright test

real example:
CI fails rarely when a lockfile exists because version drift between developer laptops and the pipeline disappears.
